summary: NSG rule AllowSshInbound on nsg-app permits inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0 to subnet snet-app, exposing SSH management access to the public internet.

evidence.detail: direction=Inbound, access=Allow, protocol=Tcp, destinationPortRange=22, sourceAddressPrefix=0.0.0.0/0, priority=100
nic-app01 is a member of nsg-app and has private IP 10.20.1.4 in snet-app

reasoning.description: Rule AllowSshInbound is an Allow rule at priority 100 with no lower-priority rule for TCP/22 that would override it.
Source address prefix 0.0.0.0/0 matches any internet-routable source address.
nic-app01 is directly associated with nsg-app, so the rule is enforced on its traffic.

assumptions: No higher-priority Deny rule targeting TCP/22 exists on nsg-app's default_security_rules (default rules are always priority >= 65000, below this custom rule's priority 100).
limitations: Does not evaluate whether a subnet-level Azure Firewall or NVA route intercepts this traffic before it reaches nic-app01 -- see route.azure-route-to-onprem.json for the subnet's UDR, which does not cover 0.0.0.0/0 and therefore does not mitigate this finding.
remediation: Restrict AllowSshInbound's source_address_prefix to a known management CIDR (e.g. a bastion subnet or VPN client range) instead of 0.0.0.0/0, or replace direct SSH exposure with Azure Bastion.
